title: P0 — Windows-native runtime: kernel-HANDLE artifact security + native Codex executor
description: Windows-native closure of the two post-PR#115 execution blockers. WS-A: new src/pair/win32-object-io.ts binds every governed filesystem step to the kernel HANDLE of the opened object (CreateFileW/NtCreateFile with RootDirectory-relative opens = literal /proc/self/fd/<fd>/<name> parity, GetFinalPathNameByHandleW for opened-object canonical path, FileIdInfo identity, FileRenameInformationEx atomic no-replace publish, FILE_DELETE_ON_CLOSE temp discipline, FlushFileBuffers real dir durability, OPEN_REPARSE_POINT = O_NOFOLLOW parity). Wired into secureReadContained (canonical.ts), CAS dir fsync (artifact-authority.ts), and dependency materialization (artifact-handoff.ts) — all POSIX paths unchanged. WS-B: codex-cli-transport resolves executables natively on win32 (PATHEXT scan + LOCALAPPDATA install dirs + env seams, prefers real .exe over .cmd shims), spawns .cmd only via COMSPEC with a metacharacter-strict argv whitelist; codex-adapter pins windows.sandbox='elevated' on win32 (real codex 0.162.0-alpha.17.2 verified: exec_command runs as CodexSandboxOffline under restricted token), adds async child error handling so spawn failures settle FAILED not TIMEOUT, preserves timeout/cancel, and supplies Windows essentials (SYSTEMROOT/USERPROFILE/LOCALAPPDATA/PATH) while still stripping ambient secrets and PAIR control flags. WS-C: LOCAL_INGEST_SUPPORTED now probes the real seam (HANDLE path qualifies win32); strict COMPLETED required — delegated-mission proof now COMPLETES on native Windows (previously ABORTED-only). POSIX-only fs-instrumentation tests in f1-r2 gated behind explicit platform skips; dir-symlink attacks use unprivileged junctions on win32. 25/25 win32-runtime adversarial + live codex file green; 43/43 goal-context green.
